name: Healthy Eating Checklist
description: A daily checklist of balanced-eating habits built around vegetables, fruit, whole grains, lean protein and less added sugar.

items.text: Fill at least half your plate with vegetables at main meals
Eat a serving of fruit as a snack instead of sweets
Include a variety of colors across the day
items.note: Different colors signal different vitamins, minerals and antioxidants.

items.text: Add leafy greens to a meal (salad, soup or stir-fry)
Keep frozen or pre-cut veg on hand for busy days
Aim for at least five servings of fruit and veg total
Choose whole-grain bread, pasta or wraps over refined white
Start the day with oats or a whole-grain cereal
Swap white rice for brown rice, quinoa or barley sometimes
Include beans, lentils or chickpeas in a meal
items.note: Legumes add fiber and plant protein at low cost.

items.text: Check that whole grain is the first ingredient on labels
Include a protein source at each meal (eggs, fish, poultry, tofu or beans)
Eat fish, especially oily fish like salmon, once or twice a week
Choose lean cuts and trim visible fat from meat
Use olive oil, nuts, seeds or avocado for healthy fats
Limit processed meats such as bacon and deli meat
items.note: Save processed meats for occasional treats rather than daily eating.

items.text: Swap sugary drinks for water, sparkling water or unsweetened tea
Read labels and compare added sugar between products
Keep chips, candy and pastries as occasional, not daily, foods
Cook more meals from whole ingredients at home
Choose plain yogurt and add your own fruit instead of pre-sweetened
items.note: Pre-sweetened products often hide several teaspoons of added sugar.

items.text: Use a smaller plate to help with portion sizes
Eat slowly and stop when comfortably full
Plan meals and a rough shopping list for the week
Limit eating in front of screens to notice fullness cues
Prep a few meals or snacks ahead for busy days
Drink water through the day and with meals
Pick one or two habits to focus on this week
Keep healthy snacks visible and treats out of sight
Forgive an off day and get back on track at the next meal
Track your habits with this printable checklist
Important: this is general information, not medical or dietary advice
items.note: For personalized guidance or a health condition, consult a doctor or registered dietitian.

faq.q: What does healthy eating actually mean?
faq.a: Healthy eating means building most meals around vegetables, fruit, whole grains, lean protein and healthy fats, while limiting added sugar, excess sodium and ultra-processed foods. Variety, balance and reasonable portions matter more than any single food.

faq.q: How many fruits and vegetables should I eat a day?
faq.a: Many health bodies suggest aiming for at least five servings of fruit and vegetables daily, filling about half your plate. More color and variety helps you cover a wider range of nutrients and fiber.

faq.q: Do I have to give up all treats?
faq.a: No. Healthy eating is about overall patterns, not perfection. You can enjoy treats in moderation as long as most of your meals are balanced and built around whole foods.

faq.q: Can I print this healthy eating checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each habit each day to build a consistent routine.
